title: Review of lab 1's xcell-evo2-S on fresh seeds 3 and 4: the planted ringed bodies divide persistently (10 and 10 persistent splits, generation 5 on both, 0 merges), better than 2 of the 3 original seeds
summary: labkit re-runs of threads/fisim-beyond-laplacian/worlds/xcell-evo2-S/world.py on fresh seeds 3 and 4, with the pack's own settings (frames 200, spf 500, t=2000, 128^2). Seed 3: 10-12 bodies, 13 splits, 10 persistent, max generation 5, 0 merges. Seed 4: 10-13 bodies, 12 splits, 10 persistent, generation 5, 0 merges. The original pack gave 11/7/6 persistent splits and generation 6/2/2. The CH membrane channel m is membrane-like on both seeds (rim/core 2.58 and 2.49, rim/outside 9.8 and 9.3, 64/65 and 66/67 individuals). The sheet shows round bodies with a membrane band dividing through dumbbells (seed 3 t~170 and t~1480). Bodies are planted (10 founders), and turnover is an imposed random disk erasure, as the claim states.

observations.I: rerun/seed3/sheet.png: 10-12 discrete round bodies persisting through t=2000
observations.D: rerun/seed3 and seed4 FACTS: 10 persistent splits each, max generation 5, 0 merges, from 10 planted founders (generation >= 3 after the founders)

verdicts.limitation: Planted founders; deaths are imposed disk erasures. I saw the m membrane band (rim/core 2.5) but did not audit whether it is a dynamically independent layer or a contour of the body, so B is not checked here.
